div.head: Dates
div.p: Everything dated has one kind of date: a council and a person's life (), a manuscript's unit, its hands and its binding (), a relation, such as an owner's from 1460 to 1520 (), and a date the text names (). A date keeps the words its source gives ("sec. IX ultimo terzo", "ERA DLXXXVII"), and what they mean: a point or a span, its bounds, its precision (a century, a year, a month, a day), whether it's circa or uncertain, and the calendar or era of its words. The application searches every date by its bounds, shows it in its words, and exchanges it in EDTF, the Extended Date/Time Format of ISO 8601-2.
Nothing in this part is required. date is common, since the editions' imprints carry one; the rest is full.

div.head: The one form
div.p: A date is written once, in one form, whatever element carries it:

list.item: its words, as the element's text, where the element has text (date, origDate, birth, floruit); a record's date may have none;

div.p: The import makes one date of them: the words, the bounds, the precision (from the EDTF, or from the bounds' form), circa and certainty (from the EDTF's marks), and the calendar. An export writes the same form. The application's date form proposes the bounds and the EDTF from the words; an encoder may write them by hand. TEI's other forms of the same date, its ISO attributes (when-iso, …), a named period (period), and the custom bounds (notBefore-custom, notAfter-custom), aren't taken: one form.
A century is the commonest date of a manuscript. The bounds follow the words: "sec. X" is 901 to 1000. Its EDTF is 09XX, which EDTF reads as 900 to 999; the checks allow the year's difference ():
A part of a century needs no EDTF: the bounds say it, and the words keep how it was said.
A circa date gives in its bounds how far the encoder, or the source, reads the circa; its EDTF keeps the year named:

An uncertain year, and the years it may be instead, is a point between bounds with its EDTF marked uncertain. The edition of the Council of Aschheim dates it "a. 756 vel 755-60"; as a record of the council:
A span has its two ends. In the records of the Council of Carthage of 397, Aurelius of Carthage flourishes from 388 to 423:
Where a span's ends are uncertain, each end has its EDTF, and the bounds hold the earliest start and the latest end:

div.head: Calendars and eras
div.p: The bounds are always in the Christian era, in the Gregorian calendar, as TEI defines them; EDTF is too. The words may reckon otherwise: by the Spanish era, 38 years ahead of the Christian, by the Julian calendar's days, by a king's years. calendar names the reckoning of the words, pointing to a calendar that the file declares once, in the profile description's calendarDesc; the bounds give what the words come to. A date without calendar reckons in the Christian era. Each declaration says what the calendar is, and may link to a description of it in target. The declarations the guide uses:

calendar.p: The Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF), ISO 8601-2: the form of the dates' custom attributes.
The Julian calendar, in which the sources give their days.
The Spanish era, which counts from 38 BC.

div.p: A day reckoned in the Julian calendar says so, and its bounds give the Gregorian day: later by 2 days in the 6th century, 3 in the 7th, 4 in the 8th and 9th, 5 in the 10th, 6 in the 11th, 7 in the 12th and 13th, each difference starting on 1 March of the century's first year. A month or a year keeps its units: "mense Augusto 822" is 0822-08, since a few days at its edges make no difference at its precision. The application shows a date in its words, and can give the Julian day back from the calendar. The Council of Valencia, 549, dates itself by the era, the king's years and the Roman day, which is 4 December in the Julian calendar:

egXML.head: ITEM VALLETANUM CONCILIUM, VI EPISCOPORUM HABITUM ERA DLXXXVII ANNO XV TEUDERICI REGIS SUB DIE II NONAS DECEMBRES

div.p: A manuscript's unit dated to the day, in a catalogue that gives the Julian day:
A calendar the file doesn't declare is an error:
The ids of the declarations are the file's own; the examples above give each its own, since the guide's ids are unique. A file usually needs edtf, and julian where it dates to the day.

constraintSpec.desc: A date's calendar and dating method point to a declared calendar.

sch:rule.sch:assert: @calendar and @datingMethod point to a calendar declared in the profile description's calendarDesc ().

div.head: What the checks require
div.p: The RelaxNG checks each bound's form. The Schematron checks that a date reads one way:

list.item: a point between bounds gives both, and a span both its ends (warnings);
no bound comes after its pair: notBefore after notAfter, or from after to (an error);
an EDTF value has EDTF's form, as this part uses it, and its datingMethod (an error);
every calendar and datingMethod points to a declared calendar (an error).

div.p: Folios and pages also have from and to (locus, biblScope, citedRange): these rules leave them alone.

constraintSpec.desc: A point between bounds gives both.

sch:rule.context: tei:*[@notBefore or @notAfter][not(self::tei:locus or self::tei:biblScope or self::tei:citedRange)]
sch:rule.sch:assert: A point between bounds gives both, @notBefore and @notAfter.

constraintSpec.desc: A span gives both its ends.

sch:rule.context: tei:*[@from or @to][not(self::tei:locus or self::tei:biblScope or self::tei:citedRange)]
sch:rule.sch:assert: A span gives both its ends, @from and @to.

constraintSpec.desc: No bound comes after its pair.

sch:rule.context: tei:*[(@notBefore and @notAfter) or (@from and @to)][not(self::tei:locus or self::tei:biblScope or self::tei:citedRange)]

sch:let.name: first
sch:let.value: for $b in (@notBefore, @from) return concat($b, substring('-01-01', string-length($b) - 3))

sch:let.name: last
sch:let.value: for $b in (@notAfter, @to) return concat($b, substring('-12-31', string-length($b) - 3))

sch:assert.test: (not(@notBefore and @notAfter) or $first[1] le $last[1]) and (not(@from and @to) or $first[last()] le $last[last()])

sch:rule.sch:assert: No bound comes after its pair: @notBefore before @notAfter, @from before @to.

constraintSpec.desc: An EDTF value has EDTF's form, and its dating method.

sch:rule.sch:assert: An EDTF value is a date (0813, 0816-08, 0813-06-13), its last digits unspecified (08XX) or itself marked circa or uncertain (~, ?, %), or a set of them ([0755,0756], [0867..0900]); and the element points to EDTF by @datingMethod="#edtf".

constraintSpec.desc: The bounds agree with the EDTF, by years.

sch:let.name: blo
sch:let.value: if ($lo castable as xs:integer) then xs:integer($lo) else ()

sch:let.name: bhi
sch:let.value: if ($hi castable as xs:integer) then xs:integer($hi) else ()

sch:let.name: point
sch:let.value: empty($wlo) or empty($blo) or empty($bhi) or (if (matches($w, '[~?%]')) then $blo le $wlo and $whi le $bhi else if (contains($w, 'X')) then abs($blo - $wlo) le 1 and abs($bhi - $whi) le 1 else $blo eq $wlo and $bhi eq $whi)

sch:let.name: bf
sch:let.value: if ($fb castable as xs:integer) then xs:integer($fb) else ()

sch:let.name: start
sch:let.value: empty($flo) or empty($bf) or (if (matches($f, '[~?%]')) then $bf le $flo else if (contains($f, 'X')) then abs($bf - $flo) le 1 else $bf eq $flo)

sch:let.name: bt
sch:let.value: if ($tb castable as xs:integer) then xs:integer($tb) else ()

sch:let.name: end
sch:let.value: empty($thi) or empty($bt) or (if (matches($t, '[~?%]')) then $thi le $bt else if (contains($t, 'X')) then abs($bt - $thi) le 1 else $bt eq $thi)

sch:rule.sch:assert: The bounds agree with the EDTF, by years: an exact date has the bounds' years, a century or decade (08XX) differs by a year at most, a circa or uncertain date lies within them.
